text:
sara_support: FYI BlueHarbor reporting intermittent 429s and auth retries this morning around their morning peak (08:30-09:15 PT). They’re on a Dedicated pool (pool-blueharbor-prod) — engineering requested an escalation to confirm right-sizing and a warmup plan.

lindsey_csm: Customer says baseline QPS ~ 180 req/s, sustained peak ~ 550 req/s for ~20m, spiky bursts to ~1.1k QPS for <2m. They expect 95% P99 latency < 220ms.

ash_telemetry: Quick paste of our metrics snapshot for the window:```
pool: pool-blueharbor-prod
avg_qps: 220
peak_qps: 1100
p99_latency: 320ms
cpu_util: 72%
gpu_util: 93%
queued_requests: spikes to 300
429_count: ~420 (08:40-08:52)
autoscale.min_replicas=2
autoscale.max_replicas=6
```

jon_eng: Looks like GPU util is pegged at 93% during peaks -> autoscaler didn’t keep up. Min replicas of 2 is too low for their steady baseline. Also seeing noisy-tenant time slices where one tenant’s long-context jobs push KV cache thrash.

kai_oncall: Any evidence of auth failures vs true 429s from rate-limiting? Logs show upstream auth success, then app-level 429s when queueing >200. So these are serving-throttles not auth-backend.

lindsey_csm: Customer mentioned billing spikes due to retries. They want concrete steps and ETA to avoid recurrence this month.

jon_eng: Quick mitigation plan: 1) increase autoscale.min_replicas to 4; 2) raise autoscale.max_replicas to 10 temporarily; 3) enable burst_capacity for pool-blueharbor-prod (if allowed in their contract); 4) add short circuit routing to fallback model variant (smaller context) for non-critical traffic.

ash_telemetry: I can patch metrics alert thresholds and enable a dashboard for them. Also recommend setting target_utilization to 70% instead of current 85%.

redwood-bot: deploybot: canary deploy queued for 2369990300 -> change autoscale config for pool-blueharbor-prod (min=4,max=10,util_target=0.7)

jon_eng: For longer term: right-size guidance — for their baseline 180 req/s (avg token length ~30), we recommend reserved slab of 6x T4-equivalent or 3x A10-equivalent with warmup traffic to reach steady KV cache. Practically: move to 4x replicas of larger instance or 8x of current small ones depending on their contract.

kai_oncall: Repro steps for eng to validate: 1) run synthetic load: `hey -qps 600 -z 10m` with mixed short/long contexts; 2) inject 2 2-min bursts at 1.2k QPS separated by 5m; 3) observe autoscale ramp, queue length, and p99. Attach synthetic script we used earlier.

sara_support: Customer is OK with a temporary quota bump + warmup window tonight (01:00-02:00 PT). We need eng ETA for the autoscale config change and a short runbook for warmup.

jon_eng: I’ll take the change. ETA 45m to apply and validate in prod Canary, then schedule warmup tonight. I’ll post validation logs here.

ash_telemetry: After autoscale change, will monitor the following metrics and add alerts: queued_requests>50 for >2m, gpu_util>85% for >3m, 429_rate>5/min.

lindsey_csm: I’ll notify the customer and confirm warmup window. Also will provide a short note about retry backoff recommendations to avoid billing amplification.

jon_eng: Post-change notes (will paste after validation): - reduced p99 to ~210ms during 10m synthetic run - no 429s when injecting bursts up to 1.05k QPS - observed slow ramp when GPU eviction happened; flagged for runtime team to look into KV cache cold start.

kai_oncall: Follow-ups: runtime team to investigate noisy tenant job pattern and implement evict-protected slots or isolation; ops to consider a soft reservation for BlueHarbor for critical hours; CS to advise customer on gradual ramp instead of aggressive retries.

sara_support: Thanks all — please post the final validated config here and I’ll close the case after CSM confirms customer acceptance. :white_check_mark:
